`fetch_pr_context` normalizes changed files to key `"path"` (`scripts/reviewer.py:4272`), but this reads `"filename"` — so every entry resolves to `""` and the whole `_COMPLEXITY_HIGH_PATH_MARKERS` signal (auth/token/crypto/`scripts/reviewer.py`/`action.yml` → HIGH) plus the single-docs LOW carve-out are dead code. Concrete failure: with `complexity-labels-enabled: true`, a 2-file `src/auth/login.py` change (+15/−3) that omits the model-assessed level gets `complexity:low` instead of the documented `complexity:high`; only the file-count/line-delta signals work. The new tests pass because their fixtures (`tests/test_findings_parser.py:83`, `:98`) use `"filename"` too — switch those to `"path"` and add one case asserting the marker path actually returns `high`.


These are raw substring matches, so `auth` hits `docs/AUTHORS.md`, `AuthorCard.astro`, or any `oauth-*` path, and `token` hits `tokenize.py` — a one-line docs edit to such a path returns `complexity:high` because this check runs *before* the `_COMPLEXITY_DOC_SUFFIXES` carve-out below, contradicting the "docs-only → typically low" contract in `.review/extension.md`. Once finding #1 is fixed this becomes live behavior. Consider matching path segments (e.g. `set(p.lower().split("/")) & marker_set`) or dropping the doc suffixes from the HIGH check.

The optional-variant schema embeds a `// optional` comment inside the ```json fence, while the same directive two rules below demands the file "MUST parse with Python `json.load()`". A CLI model that mirrors the template verbatim emits a JSON comment, `json.load` fails, and the whole findings file drops to the malformed-fallback path (losing every inline comment). Move the annotation outside the fence — e.g. `(the "complexity" field is optional)` in the prose rules.
